newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan premium up as Nomura scandal spreads to DKB.
newsitem.headline: Japan premium up as Nomura scandal spreads to DKB.

text.p: The Japan premium -- the extra cost Japanese banks pay for raising funds in the Eurodollar interbank market -- rose on Tuesday on news that prosecutors had raided the headquarters and homes of several officials of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), traders said.
They said the creditworthiness of Japanese banks in general was overshadowed by the news.
Japanese banks were paying around 5.84 percent for one-month Eurodollar deposits on Tuesday, about 0.16 percentage point above the prevailing rate.
The premium has stood at around 0.06 percentage point to 0.09 percentage point since the start of this month.

A spokesman for DKB said the bank would cooperate with the investigation, which Deputy Chief Prosecutor Kunihiro Matsuo said was linked to the probe into the Nomura Securities Co Ltd payoff and racketeer scandal.

But the bank declined to comment on media reports that it made questionable loans to racketeer Ryuichi Koike, who was arrested last week along with his younger brother Yoshinori Koike on suspicion of violating Japan's Commercial Code by taking some 50 million yen in illegal payments from Nomura.
The Commercial Code bans companies from making payments to "sokaiya", racketeers who typically extort money from companies by threatening to disrupt shareholder meetings.
Japanese newspapers said DKB holds problem loans worth 7.5 billion yen linked to Koike, and that another financial firm with close ties with DKB has Koike-linked bad loans worth 1.2 billion yen.
